places.name: The Poler's Breath

places.name: The Unmaking Yard

places.name: Teeth-Pens
sources: Lore:Dead-Water (crocodiles); Lore:Lizard-Steed; Lore:Riverbacks (osheeja gar)

why.pressures: The pens have failed twice and the village rebuilt them larger.

places.name: The Hunt Ledge

why.pressures: The offerings have got smaller as the hunting has got worse.
why.wouldChangeIf: An empty ledge would be read as the end of the hunting.

neighbours: between a village and a lair

places.name: Since-The-Tree
sources: world/sources/lore/topics/hist-placement.md R4 (bereavement is the strongest backstory)

why.founding: A village whose Hist was killed during the Umbriel passage and which has stayed put ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: Their ground is good and their reason for staying is that leaving would be a second death.
why.occupantsMotive: People with no hatching, no naming and no soul-return, keeping a village going anyway.
why.pressures: Their young are Hist-less by birth — a whole generation the province has no category for.
why.wouldChangeIf: Adoption by a neighbouring tree would dissolve them into someone else's tribe, which they have refused twice.

preferences: landforms: flood-high, any-firm-ground, oxbow
water relation: as a hist-village
neighbours: neighbours argue about taking them in

places.name: The Under-Pool

places.name: One-Spine
sources: Lore:Murkmire (platforms ascending from ground to hover above water)

why.siteAdvantages: One firm alignment across two kilometres of mire.
why.occupantsMotive: Households in a line, in an order that is also a social order.
why.pressures: The far end floods first and the far end is where the poorest live.
why.wouldChangeIf: Extending the spine would cost more than the village earns in a decade.

water relation: crosses water rather than sitting beside it

vibe.senses: still air over dead water, drum-signal at distance, sulphur off disturbed mud, the silence where birds should be

why.occupantsMotive: Blights that were not raised by anyone's fault.
why.pressures: The village that owns the field cannot afford to restake it and cannot afford not to.

places.name: The Carriers' Camp
sources: Lore:Argonian (bones brought to the dirt); Blackrose Chainbreakers (quest plan)

why.siteAdvantages: Where the poling routes converge before the walking route begins.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers, in season.
why.pressures: The Umbriel-era backlog reaches this camp too, and it is visible in the stacks.
why.wouldChangeIf: A carriers' strike would leave a season's dead unreturned.

places.name: The Fallen Meer

places.name: Dead-Water Village
sources: Lore:Dead-Water Village
Lore:Naga-Kur
world/sources/lore/topics/hist-placement.md (blue flowers, not red)

why.founding: The Naga-Kur's seat: the tribe built for surviving the worst thing in the swamp, around the tree that made them.

why.occupantsMotive: A tribe whose whole discipline — grave rite, watch, blight-craft — is organised around the dead not staying down.
why.pressures: Umbriel's legacy is exactly their enemy, and they have not stopped preparing; their kin on the roads are tribeless and their reputation suffers for it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the blight pressure stopped, the tribe would have no reason for the discipline that defines it.

places.name: The Chimney

why.occupantsMotive: What was sealed in it, now not sealed in it.
why.pressures: It is spreading through the flooded lower halls and out into the swamp.
why.wouldChangeIf: Sealing it again is possible and nobody has the nerve.

places.name: The Jam
sources: region grammar: deep river corridor; Lore:Seafalls; the arterial class needs its own hazards

why.founding: A permanent logjam that has become a landform.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the channel narrows and every flood adds to the pile.
why.occupantsMotive: A portage crew, and whatever dens inside the jam.
why.pressures: The jam is now holding back a head of water nobody has measured.
why.wouldChangeIf: A breach would flood four villages downstream.

preferences: landforms: waterfall, gorge, ravine, water-narrows, confluence
water relation: the water IS the hazard
neighbours: forces every boat route to stop; a portage or a ferry always answers it

why.pressures: It is the physical demonstration of the main quest's premise, standing in the world before the quest names it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reconnection is possible in principle and nobody knows how.

why.founding: An Imperial-era cargo barge that went down in the narrows with its load aboard.
why.siteAdvantages: It sank in the deep of the bend and has never shifted.
why.occupantsMotive: Fish, and divers who take a little at a time.
why.pressures: The cargo is bonded goods and a company that no longer exists still legally owns them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry cycle would expose the deck and end the slow looting.
